newsitem.title: UK: Granada says Forte integration on target.
newsitem.headline: Granada says Forte integration on target.

text.p: British media and leisure group Granada said on Wednesday that it would deliver on its promise to improve profits at its acquistion Forte by over 100 million pounds ($167.5 million) per annum from 1996/97.

Granada, which increased 1995/96 full-year profit before tax and exceptional items by 37 percent to 480 million pounds, said it planned to complete the disposal of 17 luxury hotels formerly owned by Forte by early 1997.
Granada acquired family-controlled hotel and catering empire Forte for 3.9 billion pounds ($6.53 billion) in January after a bitter takeover battle.

"We have already improved (Forte) profitability by approaching 40 million pounds and I am confident that, as promised during the bid, we will have improved ongoing profits at Forte, as part of the Granada Group, by over 100 million pounds per annum from 1996/97," Chief Executive Charles Allen said in a statement.
Chairman Gerry Robinson said there was substantial interest from a wide range of potential purchasers of the luxury hotels.
Granada sold the first of the 17 properties on Tuesday when Mandarin Oriental International Ltd bought London's Hyde Park Hotel for 86 million pounds. ($1=.5970 Pound)
